subject: Automotive & EVs
title: EVs and the Power Grid
description: A quick, practical guide to EVs and the Power Grid.

hook.text: Critics say mass EV adoption will crash the power grid. The reality is more nuanced.

buildup.text: If every US car went electric overnight, electricity demand would rise about 25–30%.

discovery.text: But the switch won't be overnight. Utilities have years to add capacity as EV adoption grows gradually.

twist.text: Most charging happens at night when grid demand is lowest. EVs actually help balance the daily load.

climax.text: Smart charging and time-of-use rates can shift EV demand to off-peak hours automatically.

punchline.text: EVs stress the grid less than most people assume.

quiz.question: When do most EV owners charge their cars?
